releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.18
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 12.18.0 packs, publishes, and installs packages with platform variants on pnpr registries. It also adds per-skill approval of agent skills and `pnpm store add` for offline installs from downloaded tarballs. Repeat installs and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer read the `package.json` of unchanged workspace projects. The release fixes several peer dependency resolution bugs too.

### Minor Changes

#### Agent skills

- pnpm now names the link to a dependency's agent skill after the skill alone. A skill that the `@acme/kit` package ships in `skills/auth/` is linked as `.claude/skills/auth`, not `.claude/skills/pnpm-@acme+kit-auth`. The next install replaces links with the old names. pnpm lists the linked skills in a `# pnpm` block of each agent skill directory's `.gitignore` [#17455](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/17455).

  When two approved packages ship a skill of the same name, or the name is already taken in an agent skill directory, pnpm links the skill as `pnpm-<package>-<skill>`. Before, the install failed.

- `pnpm approve` now asks which agent skills to link when a package ships more than one. pnpm records the chosen skills as a list, such as `permissions.<pkg>.skills: [guide, migrate]`, and does not offer the other skills for approval again. The first time a project approves a skill, `pnpm approve` also asks which agent directories to link skills into, and records the answer under `skills.dirs`.

- pnpm links agent skills nested in category directories, such as `skills/engineering/implement/SKILL.md`, up to three levels below `skills/`. Before, it linked only the skills directly under `skills/`.

#### Platform variants

These features need a registry declared with `serverType: pnpr`.

- `pnpm pack` packs one archive per entry of `publishConfig.variants`, each platform variant as `<name>-<version>~<tag>.tgz`. `pnpm pack --variant <target>` packs only the archive whose entry lists that target. `pnpm pack --json` prints the `integrity` and `size` of every archive it writes.

- `pnpm publish` publishes a package's `publishConfig.variants`. pnpm uploads every archive before the publish request that references them. Publishing variants to any other registry is refused unless `--no-variants` is given, which publishes only the archive that targets `any`.

- `pnpm publish --upload-variant <target>` uploads the archive of one `publishConfig.variants` entry to the registry's staging area and prints `<target>=<integrity>`. `pnpm publish --variant-integrity <target>=<integrity>` then publishes the version from archives that other jobs uploaded. With `--recursive`, each value names its package as `<name>~<target>=<integrity>`.

- `pnpm publish -r --batch` now uploads each package archive on its own request and skips archives the registry already holds, so the batch request no longer grows with the archives it publishes. A batch of more than 256 packages still carries every archive inline. Packages with `publishConfig.variants` can be publ
…(truncated)

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 11.28.11
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 11.28.11 fixes frozen installs with `excludeLinksFromLockfile`, `pnpm link` in workspaces, `pnpm deploy` with dangling symlinks, and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` starting needless installs.

### Patch Changes

#### Installing packages

* `pnpm deploy` now keeps a symlink in the project whose target is missing from the source, such as a link into a `node_modules` directory that was removed after the build. Deploy used to fail with `ENOENT` on such a link [#17571](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17571).

* A package with `bundledDependencies` and a build script now keeps its bundled dependencies when it is restored from the side-effects cache [#17523](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17523).

* `pnpm install` now links the runtime that an earlier `pnpm install --no-runtime` skipped [#17542](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17542).

* Commands of a package whose `bin` paths contain excess parent directory segments, such as `../dist/cli.js`, are no longer missing. Such paths now resolve inside the package [#17586](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17586).

* Generated POSIX shell shims now quote their paths, so shell special characters in a path stay literal.

* A repeat `pnpm install` now rewrites the bin shims after `extendNodePath` changes. Before, it reported "Already up to date" and the shims kept the `NODE_PATH` of the previous setting.

#### Lockfile and resolution

* `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts the lockfile it wrote with `excludeLinksFromLockfile` and `linkWorkspacePackages` on, when a project depends on a workspace package through a plain version range or a `catalog:` entry. It used to fail with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`.

* `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm approve-builds`, and `pnpm rebuild` now accept a lockfile that resolves a `*` dependency to a prerelease `latest` version. pnpm wrote such a lockfile and then reported it as outdated [#17594](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17594).

* Packages from the default registry keep plain lockfile keys, even when a prefix such as `npmjs` points at the registry set as `registry`. A dependency written with such a prefix shares the plain entry of the same package. The next install rewrites keys that earlier versions qualified this way [#17575](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17575).

* Relative local paths in root `overrides` now resolve from the workspace root when each project has its own lockfile [#17691](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17691).

  Installing a local directory dependency no longer fails when another project's install is writing a lockfile in that directory.

* Peer deduplication no longer gives a project different copies of a dependency across direct and transitive paths when an optional peer has no provider [#17666](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17666).

* A Node.js version range such as `>=26.13`, for example in `devEngines.runtime`, now resolves to the newest stable release that satisfies it. pnpm picks a prerelease only whe
…(truncated)

prs.title: feat(pnpr)!: remove the documents metadata backend
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Second of two PRs. It removes pnpr's `documents` metadata backend, so SQL metadata is the only one: SQLite in the storage directory by default, or the database `metadata.url` names (`sqlite:` or libSQL). It follows #17638, which moved the tests, fixtures, mocks, and helpers off documents.

- **Config**: `MetadataBackend::Documents` is gone. A config that still sets `metadata.backend` (any value) is refused, and the error points at `metadata.url`. An `s3:` hosted store that hosts packages and has no `metadata.url` used to fall back to documents in the bucket. It is now refused, with a pointer at a libSQL URL. A tier that hosts no packages, such as an artifact-only one, still needs no metadata URL.
- **Storage**: the documents implementation is gone. `PackageMetadata` now has a single implementation, so it becomes a struct (the former `SqlView`). The documents-only defaults go with it: the `read_version` that rendered the whole view, `read_release_record` that held nothing, and `read_view_at_least` that ignored the generation. `Storage::new` takes the metadata backend and `with_metadata` is gone. `sql_metadata()` always returns the database, and `PackageView.generation` is always set. The SQLite and libSQL adapter trait stays. `HostedBackend::list_package_names` goes, because only documents listed packages from files.
- **Publish journal**: only the documents backend committed through it, so it goes too. That covers `pnpr_storage::journal`, `merge_journaled_packumen
…(truncated)

feat(pnpr): let workload credentials stage archives and commit batches
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Part of the stack that implements publishing platform variants ([platform-variants RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-platform-variants.md), Implementation step 6). Independent of pnpm/pnpm#17648; based on `main`.

In the RFC's CI flow, each matrix job uploads its archive to the staging endpoint and a release job commits them all, every job holding the same trusted-publishing (OIDC workload) binding. Until now workload credentials could only send a single-package `PUT` to a configured package. They now may also:

- `PUT` and `HEAD` `/-/pnpr/v0/artifacts/blob` (staging is per principal);
- `PUT` `/-/pnpr/v0/publish` (the batch commit).

The authentication middleware cannot see a batch's entries, so it records a `WorkloadScope` in the request extensions. The batch handler then refuses an entry from another ecosystem, for another package, or one that resolves to another registry than the workload's (`403`).

A workload addresses its named registry (`/npm/~<registry>/`), and pnpm resolves the staging and batch endpoints relative to the registry URL. Both routes were mounted only at the server root and `/npm/`, so they are now also mounted under `/npm/~<registry>/`. A batch sent there publishes its npm entries through that registry, as a single-package `PUT` to that address does. Staged archives stay per principal, whichever address they went through.

…(truncated)

prs.title: feat(pnpr): find variants from their tag-named attachments
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

First PR of the stack that implements publishing platform variants, as specified in [the platform-variants RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-platform-variants.md) (Implementation step 6, pnpr side). Related to pnpm/rfcs#69.

A variant is now named by its tag itself, `+` included, and found from its attachment `<basename>-<version>~<tag>.tgz` alone:

- The request no longer carries `versions[<version>].pnprVariants` (pnpm/rfcs#70). A variant attachment declares its `.tgz` `integrity` beside `data`, or alone for a staged archive. pnpr rejects a `~<tag>` attachment that has no integrity, or that names a version the request does not describe.

- pnpr derives the tag from the archive's `variant` field and rejects the version when it differs from the tag that names the archive.
- A tag is at most 128 bytes (`MAX_VARIANT_TAG_BYTES` in `pnpm-platform-variants`, also enforced by the shared route check). pnpr refuses a longer one before it reads any archive.
- The free-form label is gone: the stored variant no longer keeps a `label`, and its blob name and route both derive from the tag. pnpr is pre-1.0, so stored variants with a label are not migrated.

The rest of the stack: workload credentials for staging and batch commits, versions without a primary archive, provenance subjects and variant `purl`s, then pnpm's publisher side.

Tests: `pnpm test:rust` over every `pnpr-*` crate plus `pnpm-registry-mock` and `pnpm-platform-variants` (1990 passed). 
…(truncated)

prs.title: test(run): settle records before gate check
feat(pnpr): check that provenance names every archive of a version
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Part of the stack that implements publishing platform variants ([platform-variants RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-platform-variants.md), Implementation step 6). Follows pnpm/pnpm#17648 (variants named by their tag-named attachments, merged).

**Provenance names every archive.** The RFC requires a version's provenance statement to name every archive the version publishes, so no archive enters the version outside it. pnpr reads the in-toto statement from the DSSE envelope of a version's `.sigstore` bundle (JSON or base64 JSON). It rejects the version (`400`) unless the statement has a subject for:

- the primary `.tgz`, named by the version's PURL, such as `pkg:npm/%40acme/fast@1.0.0`;
- each variant's `.tgz`, named by the same PURL with a `variant` qualifier, such as `pkg:npm/%40acme/fast@1.0.0?variant=linux-x64%2Blinux-x64-musl` (`+` is always `%2B`);

each with the `.tgz` SHA-512 npm provenance uses. The bundle must carry an in-toto statement (v1, or the v0.1 older npm provenance uses) in an `application/vnd.in-toto+json` DSSE payload. The payload may be standard or URL-safe base64, padded or not, as DSSE allows, and an unnamed subject is skipped. An archive is named only by a digest known to be its own: the bytes are verified against whichever SHA-512 their integrity carries, so an archive whose integrity carries more than one SHA-512 cannot be named and is refused. A subject's name and version compare by their canonical spelling, sin

prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes pnpm/pnpm#17665. With the global virtual store on, the slot version segment came straight from the lockfile key, so a named-registry package like `is-number@work:7.0.0` got a `<store>/links/@/is-number/work:7.0.0/<hash>` slot. Windows rejects the `:` with os error 123. The segment now uses the bare semver of a registry-qualified version, the same `7.0.0` v11 gets from `dp.parse`. The registry stays in the graph hash through the package id, so slots from different registries still don't collide.

prs.title: feat(install): decide an install with a pnpmfile from the recorded manifests
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Part of pnpm/tasks#256. `pnpm install` in an up-to-date workspace with a pnpmfile or `configDependencies` no longer reads the `package.json` of each project whose file did not change since the last install.

The CLI's pre-runtime fast path, which pnpm/pnpm#17637 taught to decide from the workspace state's manifest records, declines while a pnpmfile or a declared config dependency could still change the configuration. It runs before the config dependencies are installed and the `updateConfig` hooks run. Such workspaces therefore went through the whole install pipeline: config setup, then discovery that parses every project manifest, then `Install::run`'s own up-to-date check.

Now the install pipeline tries the fast path again right after the config setup, before discovery:

- **When:** it runs only when one of those config-time gates applied, since otherwise the pre-runtime attempt already ran with the same inputs. The other gates still apply.
- **Not for hoisted pnpmfiles:** it declines a hoisted install with a pnpmfile. The install turns its own shortcut off there when the pnpmfile declares custom fetchers (`check_custom_fetcher_reuse`), and telling needs the hooks loaded.
- **Not for malformed declarations:** it leaves a manifest that fails `validate_dependency_types` to the install, which refuses its shortcut for one.
- **Workspace package patterns:** the fast path's discovery now honors `--workspace-packages`, as the install's own does. The pre-runtime path s
…(truncated)

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Part of the stack that implements publishing platform variants ([platform-variants RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-platform-variants.md) with pnpm/rfcs#70, Implementation step 6). Follows pnpm/pnpm#17651 (merged).

**A version with variants and no `any` archive.** A publisher whose declaration has no entry targeting `any` sends the version with no `dist` and no plain attachment, only `~<tag>` variant attachments. pnpr now accepts that:

- The submitted manifest is normalized as an archive's is, and it and every variant must name the URL's package and the version key. The derived version has no build metadata, so a key with the `+r<N>` reserved for revisions is refused. Variants published with an `any` archive are held to the same identity.
- The variants are checked against the submitted manifest: name, version and peers.
- A provenance statement may accompany the version; npm's documents keep its attestations on the generated archive's `dist`.
- pnpr generates the minimal archive that npm's documents point to as `dist.tarball`. Its `package.json` has the version's name and version and the union of the variants' `os`, `cpu` and Linux `libc`; a Linux platform without a `libc` counts as glibc, and a `wasm32` variant leaves all three out. It is packed deterministically: fixed tar headers, gzip mtime 0, sorted values.
- It is written through the publish's own slot path, so a `tarballs: tar` registry stores its tar.

prs.title: fix(deps-resolver): settle child variants before peer deduplication
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix peer deduplication splitting a project's direct dependency from the same dependency reached through another package when an optional peer is absent. Apply the fix to both CLI implementations.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17666.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Require matching child variants before collapsing peer dependents. Recursive
compatibility could independently choose incompatible targets for a child
and its parent, giving one project two instances of the same dependency.

Retain all surviving variants for subsequent rounds, stop when no variant
collapses, and compose replacement maps so importer references reach the
final survivor. Use an iterative loop for the rounds. When a cycle prevents child-first
progress, collapse one recursively compatible pair per independent cyclic
component and resume those rounds. Defer parents of changed components.
Process dependency components before their parents when selecting that pair.
Reuse the peer walker's iterative component pass and the graph sequencer's
component helper. Index incoming edges so each round rewrites references to collapsed paths
without scanning unrelated nodes.

Add synthetic regression coverage in both implementations. Declare serde's
rc feature in resolver-base, whose serialized manifest contains Arc<Value>,
so scoped resolver builds do not depend on workspace feature unification.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17666.
```

- [x] I checked the referenced issue and verified that none of the PRs already li
…(truncated)

prs.title: feat(publish): publish a version with its platform variants
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

The pnpm side of publishing platform variants, part 2 ([platform-variants RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-platform-variants.md#sending-a-version-with-variants) with pnpm/rfcs#70). Follows the pack PR, pnpm/pnpm#17657 (merged).

**Single-machine `pnpm publish`.** For a package that declares `publishConfig.variants`, pnpm packs every archive and publishes them as one version to a registry declared with `serverType: pnpr`:

- It stages every archive by its integrity before the document (`HEAD`, then `PUT` when missing), reusing the batch path's staging client.
- It sends the usual `PUT <registry>/<name>` document. The document references the `any` archive as `<name>-<version>.tgz` and each platform variant as `<name>-<version>~<tag>.tgz`, each with `integrity` and `length` and no `data`.
- A version without an `any` entry is sent with no `dist` and no plain attachment. pnpr generates the archive npm's documents point to (pnpm/pnpm#17654).
- Publishing variants to any other registry is refused, also in a dry run: a version published without its variants cannot get them later. `pnpm publish --no-variants` publishes only the `any` archive instead.
- `--dry-run` runs every check and sends nothing.
- Provenance for a version with variants is refused before any archive is staged, in a dry run too, with a hint to pass `--no-provenance` (pnpm/pnpm#17660 lifts it).

prs.title: fix(install): verify injected workspace type peers
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Frozen installs now verify injected workspace dependencies with the same manifest hook chain used during resolution when `addMissingPeerTypes` is enabled. This accepts the lockfile written by the preceding install and preserves `readPackage` changes to peers.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17668.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
The resolver adds optional type peers before running readPackage on an
injected workspace dependency. Freshness verification used the importer
manifest, which lacked those inferred peers.

Retain the project manifests before importer hooks. The existing directory
manifest walk uses that source and the resolver's ordered hook chain when
addMissingPeerTypes is enabled. Only reachable directory dependencies are
transformed. Importer manifests remain unchanged, since inferred peers on
an importer would become install requirements.

Cover normal install followed by frozen install with shared and per-project
lockfiles, including hooks that remove an inferred type peer or add a peer.
Isolate the existing external-importer fixture from ancestor workspaces.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17668.
```

## Checklist

- [x] I checked the referenced issue and verified that none of the PRs already linked to it solves it.
- [x] New features are implemented only in the Rust pnpm v12 CLI. Bug fixes are implemented in every affected version.
- [x] Added a changeset for the affected published package.
- [x] Added or updated tests.
- [x] Updated the documentation if needed. Existing docu

prs.title: feat(install): decide a workspace with a lockfile per project from the records
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Part of pnpm/tasks#256. `pnpm install` in an up-to-date workspace with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` now finishes without running the install of each project, and without reading the `package.json` of projects whose files did not change.

The CLI fast path declined this mode outright ("every workspace project has its own lockfile"). Each project keeps its own lockfile and its own workspace state, so a workspace-level check could not speak for them. The install ran its per-project loop after discovery parsed every manifest. Each project's run then made its own up-to-date check.

The fast path now handles the mode itself (`install_already_up_to_date_per_project`):

1. List the projects without reading them (`find_workspace_project_manifests`), honoring `--workspace-packages`.
2. For each listed directory that holds a manifest:
   - anchor the configuration to it (`anchor_dedicated_project`) and load its own state;
   - rebuild its manifest from that state's record, as in pnpm/pnpm#17637, or take the manifest the command read for its own directory.
3. Run each project's check as its run in the loop would. The project is the only importer, and the other projects are the ones whose commands it links (`dedicated_bin_projects`).
4. Only once every project is up to date, register each one in the store, as each run does.

Any project that cannot be decided sends the install to the loop as before. That covers a missing state, an unusable record, a failed check, or a malf
…(truncated)

prs.title: feat(publish): upload variants from several machines and publish them by integrity
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:

The pnpm side of publishing platform variants, part 3 ([platform-variants RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-platform-variants.md#uploading-variants-from-several-machines) with pnpm/rfcs#70). Based on the publish PR (part 2, pnpm/pnpm#17658).

**`pnpm publish --upload-variant <target>`** runs on the machine that built an archive, such as one job of a CI matrix:

- It prints `<target>=<integrity>` per archive and nothing else on stdout. With `--json` it prints the package's name and version, and each archive's tag, targets and integrity.
- It publishes nothing, needs a registry declared `serverType: pnpr`, and refuses `--provenance`, since the committing job signs one statement for every archive.
- With `--dry-run` it packs, checks and prints, and uploads nothing.

- It packs none of the package's archives, and derives the version's manifest from the declaration.

prs.title: feat(publish): sign one provenance statement for every archive of a version
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

The pnpm side of publishing platform variants, part 4 ([platform-variants RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/blob/main/pnpr/text/0000-platform-variants.md#dry-runs-provenance-and-retries) with pnpm/rfcs#70). Based on the upload PR (pnpm/pnpm#17659).

With `--provenance`, a version with platform variants is published with one statement whose subjects are every archive it publishes, each with its `.tgz` SHA-512:

prs.title: fix: upgrade serde-saphyr to 2.1.0
prs.author: kairosci
prs.body:
## Summary

Upgrade serde-saphyr to 2.1.0 and adapt YAML parsing to its fallible scanner and token API. Preserve lockfile output and handle comment-only workspace and configuration files. Closes pnpm/tasks#258.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Upgrade serde-saphyr to 2.1.0. Adapt scanner and token handling, and treat comment-only YAML as empty where callers use defaults. Preserve lockfile serialization. Closes pnpm/tasks#258.
```

## Checklist

- [x] I checked the referenced issue and verified that none of the PRs already linked to it solves it.
- [x] Added or updated tests.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Empty and comment-only YAML files now load as empty configuration, workspace manifests, and settings instead of failing.
  * Explicit `null` values in supported configuration fields use their defaults. Invalid YAML and unknown configuration keys continue to be rejected.

`pnpm -r publish --batch` now publishes packages that declare `publishConfig.variants` to a registry declared `serverType: pnpr`, instead of refusing them ([platform variants RFC](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/pull/69)). ## Summary

`supportedArchitectures` platform-list entries are now parsed by the platform-tag parser that package variants and pnpr share (`pnpm_platform_variants::Platform::parse_tag`), as the [platform variants RFC](pnpr/text/0000-platform-variants.md#install) specifies. An entry can now state:

The tag parser is the one source of truth. The spellings pnpm read before tags are rewritten into the tag they name before it parses them:

| Older spelling | Tag |

| `current` | unchanged |

## Summary

This implements the fetch half of the [platform variants RFC](pnpr/text/0000-platform-variants.md#install)'s `supportedArchitectures` rules. With `supportedArchitectures` set, an install of a registry package with platform variants also fetches into the store, without linking them:

- every platform variant that matches one of the listed platforms (`Purpose::Fetch`: for a platform other than the host, a floor or ABI it does not state counts as met);

- `VariationsResolution::fetched_for(platform)` in the lockfile crate gives the archives one platform keeps.
- `install_package_by_snapshot/fetch/stored_variants.rs` expands `supportedArchitectures` into platforms. It fetches each archive they keep, except the linked one, through the same tarball path, so each lands in the CAS and the store index.
- `variant_for_host` also returns the selected archive, and `archive_fetch` builds the fetch for any one archive.

## Summary

Implements the link rule of the [platform variants RFC](pnpr/text/0000-platform-variants.md#install). When `supportedArchitectures` names exactly one platform and not `current`, a package with platform variants links that platform's variant, together with the dependencies that variant declares. The aim is preparing a `node_modules` for another machine. A list names one platform by one entry. The `{os, cpu, libc}` form names one when `os` and `cpu` each hold one value and no axis says `current`; an unset `libc` keeps that form's meaning, the host's C library. ## Summary

Adds the "Leaky-API check" item of pnpm/tasks#253 to the `crate-layers` tool. The other open items of that task are not part of this PR.

A crate leaks a dependency when a public signature names one of the dependency's items and the crate does not re-export it with `pub use`. Every caller that uses the signature then has to depend on that crate as well.

- `crate-layers leaks` lists each leak and how many crates depend on both sides. `--crate <name>` lists the leaked items and those crates. `--baseline` prints the table.

## Summary

This is the last part of `supportedArchitectures` for platform variants (pnpm/rfcs#69, "Install"). Every install, and `pnpm fetch`, now stores the archives the listed platforms keep together with the packages those archives depend on. Nothing extra is linked.

- **One store-only pass.** It runs after the virtual store is materialized, warm or cold, so a platform added to `supportedArchitectures` is picked up by the next install, including one that reuses every slot. `pnpm fetch` runs the same frozen install pipeline, so it follows the same rule.
- **The walk** (`current_lockfile::platform_archives`). For each listed platform, it starts at the installed projects. - **The fetch** (`InstallPackageBySnapshot::store_archives`). It downloads the kept archives concurrently, bounded by the client's per-host limit, through the existing tarball path. An archive the store already holds is read from the store index, not downloaded again.

## Summary

With `autoInstallPeers: true`, a missing optional peer could be resolved from a version that only another workspace project depends on. The reproduction in https://github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/16666: `app` depends on `webpack`, `tooling` has `webpack-cli` in `devDependencies`, and `app`'s production graph picks up `webpack-cli → webpack-dev-server → selfsigned → node-forge`.

This PR has two parts:

1. **Fix (v11 and v12):** with `dedupePeerDependents: false`, optional peers now come only from the project's own dependency graph (plus the workspace root with `resolvePeersFromWorkspaceRoot`). The optional-peer fill exists only to deduplicate, so it now respects the opt-out. The single-project case from pnpm/pnpm#12266 keeps working.
2. **New setting (v12 only):** `projectScopedOptionalPeers: true` applies the same project-scoped rule while `dedupePeerDependents` stays on. Required peers are still reused across projects, and variants are still deduplicated, except that a variant never collapses into one that resolves an optional peer it lacks. Without that guard, the dedupe pass hands another project's optional peer back to the project (the `webpack`/`esbuild` example in the `dedupePeerDependents` docs). The plan is to make this the default in the next major and then remove the setting.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

On libSQL, a publish refused at its commit left its archives in place (pnpm/pnpm#17674), and nothing could collect them while replicas keep publishing. Every archive was stored under its public filename, so a removal could race a later publish that reused that same key.

This PR stores hosted archives content-addressed and fences every removal in the metadata database, with no timing assumption.

**Storage model** (SQL schema `0.2`):
- An archive is stored under `<integrity>.<n>`: the identity of its bytes plus an incarnation number. Identical bytes are stored once per org and ecosystem, across versions, packages and image repositories.
- `blobs` holds each integrity's current incarnation and its state: `live`, `reclaiming` or `gone`.
- `artifact_blobs` maps every published file to the integrity it is stored as. It is written in the publish commit, and npm version removal deletes its rows in that same commit.
- Reads resolve a package's file through the mapping, from the replica within its freshness bound. Tarball, variant, attestation, PyPI, Cargo and OCI URLs don't change.

**Publish:**
- The read a publish already makes before promotion also looks up its integrities.
- A `live` incarnation is reused, and nothing is uploaded.
- An absent or retired integrity is uploaded as the next incarnation. Two publishers that pick the same incarnation write identical bytes to the same key.
